tools.title: The toolbox
tools.lede: What it takes to read a bus, forge a frame, probe a chip or capture a radio signal. The well-known public tools, grouped by use, with what each one does.
tools.note: Reference list for learning. None of these tools is run here.
hero.title: How to attack
hero.lede: A modern vehicle is a dozen computers talking over the same wire. Pick an attack: see where it gets in, how it travels, and what a defence actually blocks.
hero.ctx1post: of attacks are carried out remotely.
hero.ctx2post: go through telematics, cloud or APIs.
fig.caption: Top-down view. Four domains, one network, joined by the central gateway. The identifiers and frames shown are teaching examples.
fig.alt: Top-down plan of a vehicle: ECUs, communication buses coloured by domain, and a central gateway.

catalog.title: Catalogue
catalog.hint: Thirty attacks, from the CAN bus to Ethernet and charging.
cm.title: Replay the attack with a defence on
cm.sub: Each defence has a precise scope. Turn one on and watch what changes on the schematic.
footer.p1: A tool for understanding and awareness. No real attack is carried out: everything is based on publicly documented mechanisms (Car Hacker's Handbook, UNECE R155 / R156, ISO/SAE 21434, Upstream 2025 report). No data is sent, no network is touched.
footer.p2: The CAN identifiers and frames shown are teaching examples, not a real manufacturer's values.
notice.frOnly: The detailed attack sheets are currently in French.
